request.deadline: 2026-2027; exact milestone dates not stated in document
deliverables: Peras v1 mainnet readiness including production cryptography, KillSwitch, hard-fork readiness, support, and maintenance
History Expiry partial-history node work intended to reduce SPO storage costs
Conformance Testing framework extensions for Peras and Leios
Ready-for-activation deliverables including merged code, reproducible releases, runbooks, benchmarks, and governance-action packages
Public demos at least every two months, regular website status updates, Discord engagement, and Slack coordination
request.recipient: Intersect 2025 treasury reserve contract stake address stake17xzc8pt7fgf0lc0x7eq6z7z6puhsxmzktna7dluahrj6g6ghh5qjr, with Tweag by Modus Create as delivery entity.
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Tweag by Modus Create's delivery of three Cardano core infrastructure work packages over 2026-2027, administered by Intersect.

claims.claim: The proposal requests ₳18,263,496.00, stated as USD $4,565,874.00, for three Cardano infrastructure work packages delivered over 2026-2027.
Peras v1 is presented as enabling faster finality of about 2 minutes versus about 12 minutes today.

History Expiry is presented as necessary because Leios-driven throughput could cause SPO disk usage to surge to about 1 GB per hour at 100-1000 TPS, making full-history requirements economically prohibitive.
The three work packages are described as interdependent parts of a single delivery pipeline rather than separable modules.
The budget is said to be based on a $176/hour average market rate for senior Cardano infrastructure engineers and a conservative ADA/USD conversion rate of 0.25 based on a five-year average.
Tweag states it has worked on Cardano core infrastructure since January 2018, including leading consensus and ledger teams, implementing Ouroboros Genesis, and contributing to Peras design.

The proposal says Intersect will administer contract and audit functions using milestone-based fixed-price contracts where scope is well-defined, with milestone acceptance supported by a third-party assurer.
The proposal identifies the Intersect treasury reserve smart contract stake address and cites a transaction hash for final mainnet validation testing of the disburse action.
The proposer states that all funds not disbursed by the end of the delivery period, and unspent funds from canceled or reduced deliverables, will be returned to the Cardano Treasury.
The proposer states that the requested amount does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.

summary: The document requests a large treasury withdrawal for Tweag-delivered Cardano core infrastructure work, with Intersect administration, open-source/public tracking commitments, milestone controls, refund conditions, and several externally checkable references, but many key economic and feasibility details are asserted rather than developed in the anchor text.
